players.product: US utility - UHV transformer buyer (Hyosung HICO end customer)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results (CFO): GAAP EPS of $1.61 versus $1.50 in Q1 2025, including an after-tax charge of $43.9 million ($0.12 per share) for the FERC ROE decision refund covering the first 15-month complaint period. Excluding that charge, non-GAAP EPS was $1.73; the $0.23 per share improvement came mainly from the gas segment ($0.18, Massachusetts rate base increases and the Yankee Gas rate case), with electric transmission up $0.06 per share on continued investment in the system. Quarter was in line with expectations.
quarterly_data.figure: GAAP EPS $1.61 (vs $1.50); non-GAAP EPS $1.73; after-tax FERC ROE charge $43.9 million ($0.12 per share); electric transmission +$0.06 per share

quarterly_data.signal: FERC's March 19th decision cut the New England base transmission ROE from 10.57% to 9.57%, expected to lower Eversource's after-tax earnings by approximately $70 million for 2026. On April 30th Eversource made a Section 205 filing using FERC's own methodology with current market data, arriving at a base transmission ROE of 11.39% and raising the ROE cap on transmission investments to 12.89%; management expects the updated rate to be implemented towards the end of this year, subject to refund (within about 7 months of filing), with a settlement judge process possible. The refund deadline was extended to May of 2027. Guidance assumes 9.57% and will be revised on the Q4 call in February. Asked about capex flexibility if FERC rules against them, the CFO said 'that's something that we can look at.'
quarterly_data.figure: base transmission ROE 10.57% -> 9.57%; approximately $70 million 2026 after-tax earnings impact; Section 205 filing ROE 11.39%, cap 12.89%

quarterly_data.signal: Revised 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance (per the March 31st 8-K, reflecting the FERC ROE decision and the potential Aquarion sale) stated on the call as $4.57 to $4.72 per share. Reaffirmed long-term EPS growth of 5%-7% off the midpoint of the revised 2026 range, with confidence in growth towards the upper half of that target by 2028. Management separately pointed to a meaningful earnings-growth inflection driven by improved regulatory outcomes: storm cost securitization in Connecticut and New Hampshire, alternative financing, and distribution rate adjustments including the result of the CL&P rate request in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance $4.57 to $4.72; long-term growth 5%-7%, upper half by 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Grid capex: reaffirmed the 5-year utility infrastructure capital plan of $26.5 billion through 2030; CapEx of nearly $800 million through March against a 2026 forecast of $5.1 billion. Connecticut AMI (advanced metering) is not included in the plan and is pending next steps after PURA hearings. CL&P letter of intent for its first rate review in about 8 years to be filed later in May.
quarterly_data.figure: 5-year capital plan $26.5 billion; CapEx nearly $800 million through March; 2026 forecast $5.1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Regional load and new supply: the CEO cited the Massachusetts executive order referencing ISO New England projections that electricity consumption could rise by nearly 15% by 2035 and by nearly 50% by 2045, with peak demand increasing even faster. He said Eversource is 'injecting 2,600 megawatts of new power into the region' (Clean Energy Connect 1,100 megawatts, Revolution Wind 704 megawatts, Vineyard Wind over 800 megawatts). Revolution Wind is about 95% complete with commercial operation still expected in the second half of the year. Eversource purchased a 26 acre site from Constellation that will allow it to inject upwards of 2,400 megawatts of power into the region, and will partner with Enbridge on an approved natural gas pipeline enhancement.
quarterly_data.figure: consumption nearly 15% by 2035 / nearly 50% by 2045 (ISO New England projection); 2,600 megawatts new power; upwards of 2,400 megawatts via 26 acre site

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center stance (CEO, Q1 call): 'we are resisting data centers. I'm really not interested in a data center coming here. It's of no value to our residential customer. Actually, any customer. It's only gonna drive up the price of energy.'

Balance sheet and financing: Connecticut and New Hampshire storm cost securitization should recover approximately $2 billion in deferred storm costs and carrying charges within the next 12-18 months (New Hampshire portion described as probably in the '$4-$470 range' (as transcribed), targeted around late 2027). First junior subordinated notes in February brought in $1.5 billion and were more than 5 times oversubscribed. Equity needs over the 5-year forecast remain $800 million to $1.1 billion. FFO to debt at 14.2% (S&P) and 14.5% (Moody's). PURA approved the Aquarion sale; closing awaits an appeal period ending in mid-June.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $2 billion storm cost securitization; $1.5 billion junior subordinated notes; equity needs $800 million to $1.1 billion; FFO to debt 14.2% / 14.5%
